detaileddescription.para: According to cppreference.com, C++17 states: "An absolute path is a path that unambiguously identifies the location of a file without reference to an additional starting location."

In other words, the rules are: 1) POSIX style paths with nonempty root directory are absolute. 2) Windows style paths with nonempty root name and root directory are absolute. 3) No other paths are absolute.

simplesect.para: True if the path is absolute, false if it is not.

briefdescription.para: Is path absolute using GNU rules?

detaileddescription.para: GNU rules are: 1) Paths starting with a path separator are absolute. 2) Windows style paths are also absolute if they start with a character followed by ':'. 3) No other paths are absolute.

On Windows style the path "C:\Users\Default" has "C:" as root name and "\" as root directory.
Hence "C:" on Windows is absolute under GNU rules and not absolute under C++17 because it has no root directory. Likewise "/" and "" on Windows are absolute under GNU and are not absolute under C++17 due to empty root name.

parameterdescription.para: The style of path (e.g. Windows or POSIX). "native" style means to derive the style from the host.
